predecessors.text: the Kingdom of Tambapanni on the north-west coast (Tambapanni and Upatissa Nuwara, present-day Puttalam district); its infobox: 'Kingdom moved to Anuradhapura: 437 BC', 'Succeeded by: Anuradhapura…

successors.name: Chola Empire
successors.text: Sri Lanka under the Cholas: Rajendra's invasion 'ended the kingdom and left the country under the rule of the Cholas'

ledger.x: 437 BCE: Pandukabhaya founds the Anuradhapura Kingdom.
237 BCE: two South Indian horse dealers, Sena and Guththika, seize the throne and rule for 22 years.
205 BCE: the Chola prince Elara takes Anuradhapura.
161 BCE: Elara falls and Dutthagamani becomes king at Anuradhapura.
103 BCE: five Dravidian chiefs invade and rule Anuradhapura until 89 BCE ('Five Dravidian chiefs invade and rule until 89 BC, when Valagamba (89-77 BC) defeats them').
89 BCE: Valagamba defeats the five Dravidian chiefs and reigns until 77 BCE.

433: a second invasion places six South Indian rulers in control of Anuradhapura, until Dhatusena defeats Pithiya and 'regains power in 459'; the page also says Dhatusena 'founds the Moriya (Maurya) dynasty' in 455.
459: Dhatusena defeats Pithiya, regains power and founds the Moriya dynasty (the page dates the foundation 455 and the regained power 459).
473: Kashyapa I moves the capital to Sigiriya.
684: Manavanna starts the second Lambakanna dynasty, 'which lasts until Mahinda V'.

c. 993: the Cholas conquer the north. 'Chola Emperor Rajaraja I invades and conquers the north, which he names Mummudi-sola-mandalam'; the Mahinda V page: 'In 993, he fled to Ruhuna, the southern part of the country, following a large scale mutiny by his army'. The extent of 'the north' is my reading (Jaffna, the…
1017: Rajendra I destroys Anuradhapura and the kingdom ends.

wars.name: Dutthagamani's war against Elara
wars.outcome: Dutthagamani of Ruhuna defeats Elara at Vijithapura and rules nearly the whole island from Anuradhapura.

wars.name: Karikala Chola's invasion of Sri Lanka
wars.outcome: The page gives no result; it dates the invasion 'c.

wars.name: South Indian invasions under Sena I and the Sinhalese sack of Madurai
wars.outcome: Sena I's reign (833-853) 'sees further invasions and raids from South India'; in 862 Sena II's forces sack Madurai.

wars.name: Chola conquest of Anuradhapura
wars.outcome: Rajaraja I conquers the north c.

certainty.note: Mahavamsa chronology (437 BC foundation, 377 BC capital); the extent before Dutthagamani is the island minus Ruhuna by inference only.

An island coastline gives a natural limit, but the page places the real rulers' authority by province: Rajarata under the king, Ruhuna and Malaya Rata governed by officials, Ruhuna 'never fully conquered by invaders'.
